The record's constructions of maintained correction do not establish it ([ARG-042](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-042.md), Rejected), and its value is conditional on objectives, uncertainty and cost ([CLAIM-520](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-520.md)). A24's answer: "We have not established that corrigibility is unconditionally desirable." Filed because the owner asked, so it marks a real boundary. It would be argued from a declared standard, which is where [QUESTION-128](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-128.md) and [QUESTION-129](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-129.md) ask. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-512](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-512.md) v2 | The diachronic thesis faces two objections: a dilemma, that read narrowly it fails for judgments not about any organization's continuation, such as that suffering is bad, and read broadly every judgment is met vacuously as a preference between continuations unless the organizational description adds causal specificity, transfer or counterfactual discrimination; and a distinction, that evaluating a history is not prescribing its continuation, so a judgment can be determinate with no future transformation fixed | The objection to [CLAIM-518](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-518.md), put by the assistant itself in A26 §6 and A27 §10 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): "If we call every difference between possible worlds a change in some organization, then all normative judgments can be represented in these terms without learning much", and "A judgment that suffering is bad, for instance, is not obviously about organizational persistence". Unanswered. A27's three tests are the form an answer would take. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-514](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-514.md) | World-modeling is a family of resource-bounded capabilities for producing and using predictions about an environment's possibilities and consequences, each relative to a declared family of questions; a world model in the representational sense is one possible realization of them, competent behaviour can determine environmental structure without identifying any internal mechanism, and producing, maintaining and revising world-modeling capabilities are further achievements, not prerequisites of agency in general | The owner's preferred formulation at the second review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). It joins the world-model thesis, which holds that behaviour does not identify a mechanism, and its counter from Richens et al., which holds that behaviour across goals determines the dynamics. Both are kept, with each stated about a different notion of world model. It "integrates the Richens result rather than rejecting it, preserves [the] original critique of folk-model attributions, and connects both to the larger Nucleation program." Proposed: a definition and an organizing thesis, with the study [CASE-187](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-187.md) as its test. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-515](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-515.md) | Whether an organization has a cognitive property is four questions, not one: what information about the property can be recovered from its behaviour, what capabilities it can actually exercise, what mechanisms realize them, and whether it can maintain or transform those mechanisms; the four can come apart, and none should be silently substituted for another | The general principle the owner drew at the second review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): "When asking whether an organization 'has' a cognitive property, distinguish the information recoverable from its behavior, the capabilities it can actually exercise, the mechanisms realizing those capabilities, and its ability to maintain or transform those mechanisms." It was drawn from the world-model case ([CLAIM-514](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-514.md)) and judged "sufficiently general—and sufficiently testable—that it deserves an explicit place in Nucleation's research program". Proposed and interpretive: its instances are demonstrated case by case, and the generalization is not. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-518](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-518.md) v2 | Normative judgments about an organization's continuity, reform or obligations can depend on diachronic relations that descriptions of present states or terminal outcomes do not show, so specifying the relevant relations and histories can be necessary to apply them adequately; which continuations ought to follow is a further normative question, not a prerequisite of every normative judgment | From the owner's observation at U26 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), "normative judgements are only cognizable when they are relative to a judgement of whether some organization should persist or change", as narrowed at the owner's review the same day. What survives is that judgments about continuity, reform and obligation can need histories that present states and outcomes do not show. What is dropped is that every judgment needs a prescribed future: evaluating a history and fixing the admissible continuations are different problems. "Cognizable" is read as "well-defined", [CLAIM-363](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md)'s sense. Its objection is [CLAIM-512](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-512.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-519](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-519.md) v2 | Competent behaviour does not establish an internal world model: over a fixed interface and a finite horizon, an agent with no model, whose actions are looked up from the history so far, reproduces the interaction distribution of an agent that has one exactly; a policy can identify predictive structure without any particular internal component realizing it, so compression and generalization support comparing candidate architectures, and establishing an internal mechanism needs evidence that discriminates candidate implementations, such as targeted interventions | The owner's thesis at U20 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): that under the record's framework a world model is "essentially a 'folk' explanatory tool and that no such thing need explicitly be present for the external behavior to be indistinguishable from a comparable black box agent which actually did contain a world model". A20 agreed and gave the construction, with a limit the claim keeps: the attribution "sometimes ... names a genuine, interventionally identifiable computational mechanism". The construction is Block's lookup-table argument ([THEORY-092](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-092.md)) applied to agency, so it is elementary; the thesis is the reading of it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-523](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md) | For a normatively relevant discrepancy to change what an organization does, three distinct achievements are needed and any can fail while the others hold: legibility, by which the discrepancy becomes recognizable; volitional efficacy, by which a corresponding demand can move action; and correctability, by which a fitting revision can be carried out within deadline and resources; none establishes that the demand or the revision is justified, and whether the norm-satisfying histories the agent can still realize are empty depends partly on what its earlier actions destroyed | The owner's synthesis at review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). It was first filed as a dated note on [QUESTION-364](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-364.md), and filed as a claim at the owner's word ("this should probably be a new CLAIM, not hidden inside the prose of a QUESTION"). It joins three held entries, legibility ([TERM-064](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-064.md)), will-organization ([TERM-023](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-023.md)) and correctability ([TERM-085](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-085.md)), into one account of normative efficacy. It extends [CLAIM-349](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md)'s split of access, authority and action from an organization's own signals to normatively relevant discrepancies. Proposed: the separations are argued, not built. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-525](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-525.md) | Information in the sense the Simondonian readings give it, a disparity whose resolution reorders the system that takes it up, is in the line's terms a change in the interpreter or in the questions receivers can decide, not evidence about a fixed situation, so Blackwell's order leaves it out by construction and the two accounts are not rivals | The record's placing, on 2026-10-31, of the information concept in the Simondon readings (Iliadis 2013; Bencherki and Iliadis 2021; Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy 2024) against the line's Blackwell treatment. The readings' information is what reorders a receiving system; the line's is evidence about a fixed situation for a fixed receiver. The first falls in the line's interpreter channel and change of cover. It gives the readings an operational test of failing to inform, which they lack. It does not say Simondon rejects the quantitative theory, and it is not Simondon's mapping: his text is unread here. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-526](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-526.md) | Describing persons and organizations as coexisting levels of one process removes the question of how already-constituted agents add up to a collective, but not the question of levels: whether a collective variable has dynamics of its own, closed against the activity that realizes it, can be decided on a process description that presupposes no agents, is sometimes decided no, and a closed collective variable can be an aggregate that coexists with its realization while keeping none of its members' distinctions | Filed on reading Bencherki & Iliadis 2021 and Bencherki, Brummans & Vézy 2024, who hold that the "scaling up" problem "vanishes the moment communication is viewed eventfully" ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), p. 1364) because persons and organizations are "different informational levels that preserve all the characteristics of their organized components" ([LIT-1922](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md), ms. p. 21, proposition 2). The record's closure results show what survives. What vanishes is the picture of agents adding up. What remains is whether a higher variable runs on its own, which is a question about variables and is decidable. The record's own case of a closed collective variable is a sum, an aggregate, that coexists with its units, so "stages or coexisting levels" is not a dichotomy. It does not say that the agent picture is right, or that organizations are aggregates of members. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-527](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-527.md) | Viable reach, valence and emotion are three quantities in an organization, not one: an emotion is a claim to precedence, system valence is movement along the ordering that wins the negotiation, and a change in what the organization can viably reach is neither, so an organization can run ahead along its prevailing ordering while its viable reach contracts | Filed 2026-10-31 from the readings of Massumi and McKim (2009) and Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024). Massumi's affect is a transition in a body's capacitation, augmented or diminished, and the parent paper defines agency as its augmenting half. The record's affect line reads emotion as a claim to precedence (Frijda) and system valence as movement along what wins the negotiation; neither is a change in what can be done. This claim names the third quantity, viable reach, and says it can move against valence. It does not say that Massumi's capacitation is viable reach, or that more reach is better. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-528](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-528.md) | That a mechanism realizes a capacity can mean that the capacity is produced through it over time or that the capacity consists in it at a time, and interventions show only the first: a pathway whose disabling changes the capacity after a delay is a cause, can be intervened on surgically, and can be located relative to a declared boundary, whereas every intervention on a capacity that consists in its parts also changes some part along another path, so that relation is underdetermined by intervention data and is inferred by abduction or from simultaneity and settled parthood; and which of the two a given dependence is depends on the time resolution at which a description treats the parts' response as instantaneous | Filed on reading the fat-handedness debate after Craver: Baumgartner & Gebharter 2016, Baumgartner & Casini 2017 and Baumgartner, Casini & Krickel 2020. It says what their result does and does not reach in the record. [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s conclusion is causal and is left standing; [CLAIM-515](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-515.md)'s "realized", read synchronically, is not shown by discriminating interventions; and the debate's own line between causation and constitution, simultaneity, moves with the time scale, as [CLAIM-480](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md)'s chain shows. It does not say that constitution is unknowable, or that the record's organizations have constituents in the mechanists' sense. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-529](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-529.md) | An organization can be individuated without presupposing it as a declared candidate whose verdict can come out false: criteria stated on the candidate's interactions (whether benefit can be booked per member, which interactions the others depend on, what removing an interaction type does, whether its order survives release from an outside scaffold) apply to a grouping not yet assumed to be a unit, while criteria stated as members' attitudes toward the group (a goal about it, belonging, identity) make it partly constituted by being taken as one, a different individuation, unavailable where members have no such attitudes | Filed on re-reading Griesemer & Shavit 2023 ([LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)). Their abstract says transitions in individuality are hard to describe without circularity, since the features used are products of the transition, and claims a non-circular description that the body never argues. The body holds the parts of an answer, and they are of two kinds. Criteria on interactions (per-member accounting of benefit, entrenchment order, knockout of interaction types, release from a scaffold) can test a declared candidate without assuming it is a unit ([CLAIM-405](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-405.md)), and the scaffold test needs the declared boundary ([CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)). Criteria on members' attitudes toward the group (shared goal, belonging, focal goal of sustaining it) individuate constitutively, which is not the non-circular route and is unavailable for organisms without such attitudes. It does not say the paper argues this, and it leaves the presupposed lower-level units where the paper leaves them. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-530](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-530.md) | Where maintenance is realized is a question of constitutive relevance only through its parthood condition: an internal producer and an outside controller supplying the same production law as state feedback meet mutual manipulability's two manipulability conditions identically, since disabling or stimulating either changes the maintained capacities and intervening on the capacities changes the activity of either, so what puts one inside and the other outside is parthood, a boundary the experiments presuppose and do not find | The record's join of [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) with the mechanist account of constitution, from Craver and Bechtel's admission that interlevel experiments are symmetrical and show componency only prima facie ([THEORY-1287](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1287.md)). In [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s pair the bottom-up and top-down interventions come out alike for producer and controller. So the criterion separates them only by its parthood clause, which is [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s declared boundary. Proposed: the criterion's statement is taken from secondary sources. It does not say no criterion can draw the boundary. Closure, a producer that is itself maintained by what it produces, is a candidate that [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s one-variable model cannot express. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-531](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-531.md) | Generative entrenchment does not by itself give organizational closure: an entrenched core, which later interactions depend on so that perturbing it is catastrophic and perturbing them tolerable, can sit at the root of an acyclic dependency order, and where interactions turn over such an order persists only while something outside supplies its core; an organization that is both entrenched and closed has a core containing a cycle of mutual maintenance, each interaction on which is itself core unless its share of the maintenance is redundant | Filed on re-reading Griesemer & Shavit 2023 ([LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)), who mark the step from conexus to community by generative entrenchment of core interactions and then, with "Hence", by organizational closure. Entrenchment as they define it is a one-way dependency order, and a tree rooted in its core passes their knockout test; closure needs the core to depend in turn on the set. By [CLAIM-516](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-516.md), read for interactions, an acyclic order persists only on outside supply, which is their own scaffolded conexus. It does not say their communities lack closure, only that entrenchment and knockout do not show it; and it reads Wimsatt's concept only as they quote it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-532](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-532.md) | Self-formation, in the sense the record holds (the transformation dimension of a will-organization), is the production by an agent's own activity on a discrepancy it cannot yet resolve of a maintained capacity, a new distinction it can make legible or a new channel by which it can act, that outlasts the discrepancy and serves a class of later ones; it is told apart from learning an action by transfer to discrepancies of the same class after the inducing conditions are gone, and from a capacity installed or upheld from outside by interventions on the processes that produce and maintain it | The positive account A33 §7 offered, at the owner's U33 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), sharpened by the reader of U32–U33 so that it can fail. The record held self-formation as a capacity ([CLAIM-025](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-025.md), [TERM-023](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-023.md)) and what does not show it ([CLAIM-540](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-540.md): an observer's learning; [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md): recovery does not show provenance); it held no account of what self-formation produces. A33 wrote it; adopting it is the owner's call. It is a non-libertarian reading of Kane's self-forming actions ([CLAIM-022](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-022.md)'s note of 2026-11-02). The steps A33 chains, discrepancy to discrimination to response to maintained capacity to revised governance, are not a sequence ([CLAIM-474](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md)). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-533](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md) | The sensitivity that formal chaos gives a will's dynamics is not control over them: in Kane's self-forming actions, chaotic amplification keeps the outcome open, but it magnifies the agent's efforts, uncontrolled fluctuations and outside inputs alike, so what would make the outcome the agent's is how its own control couples to the amplifying directions, relative to noise and to other parties' inputs and with what feedback, which sensitivity does not supply; and under weak noise what amplification touches lasts only where it reaches the slow modes | The owner's, at U16 and U20 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02). U16: "I think there's an intuitive control theoretic connection here through the lens of controllability and sensitivity to change and chaos and slow modes." U20: "this brings us back to controllability vs sensitivity, and why I was alluding to a connection between Kane's freedom and (formal) chaos." The owner first said it at U9 of 2026-10-17 ("controllability of a system isn't binary, and neither is sensitivity to perturbation"); the controllability half was filed as [CLAIM-354](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-354.md) and [CLAIM-345](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-345.md), and the sensitivity half had no code. This is its second appearance. Its demonstrated part is [CLAIM-542](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-542.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-534](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-534.md) | A plural will's motivational integration, a dimension of freedom of will the record names and leaves unanalysed, is the extent to which the demands it maintains are jointly met, within tolerances it can recognize, across the contexts where they interact, and kept so under its own dynamics; it is neither agreement among the demands nor the dominance of one, and its parts come apart: realizability (the tolerance frontier), realization (governance frustration), maintenance (viability) and the allocation of the tolerance each demand gives up | A positive account, filed at the owner's U33 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02): "are there any positive accounts or even just hypotheses we should consider documenting on the record (even if just as proposals)?" It joins the owner's U27, "compatibility of tolerance bounds", to [CLAIM-354](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-354.md)'s "motivational integration", which the record names and does not analyse. The wording is A29's, sharpened by the reader of U27–U29; adopting it is the owner's call. Proposed: the identification is argued, and its formal half is [CLAIM-538](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-538.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-539](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-539.md) | Jennings's attention as the source of a free will has Frankfurt's two-level architecture with its upper level changed from an attitude to a process: the whole collection of an agent's interests, prioritizing, settles which first-order interest becomes effective, as a second-order volition does for Frankfurt, but by metacontrol and not by endorsement; so it inherits unchanged the objection that a manipulated organization can meet the condition, and what it adds to Frankfurt is that the process forms new interests and is a contextually emergent cause | The owner's U14 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02): "would it be fair to say Jennings theory is Frankfurt with a hat on?" Answered from [CLAIM-122](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-122.md)'s note of 2026-10-18, which separates higher-order volition, an attitude about what should be effective, from metacontrol, the machinery that alters what becomes effective. First filed as a note on [CLAIM-122](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-122.md), since the paper was unread. The owner then supplied it, and the reading ([NOTE-1508](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1508.md)) bears the claim out: attention is prioritization by a collection of interests, with no endorsement anywhere, and no historical condition. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-541](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-541.md) | Wu-wei is better read as control placed and timed where a system's own dynamics do most of the work than as the absence of control: Ott–Grebogi–Yorke control of chaos is a formal instance, in which small perturbations timed by the system's own wandering hold it on an unstable orbit, and the control, though small, continues for as long as the orbit is held; so reported effortlessness has at least three distinct sources, no conflict to override, conflict settled cheaply by learned accommodation, and conflict met as it arises by small well-timed feedback, which may feel alike and differ in mechanism | The owner's U17 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), quoting A16 on Ott–Grebogi–Yorke control: "that's very wu-wei". The first appearance was U8 of 2026-10-30, about the record's unit of explanation, noted on [CLAIM-337](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-337.md) and not filed then. This is the second, so it gets a code. The three sources are A18 §4's, joining two Proposed claims. A18 §7's statement that OGY gives "persistent" effects is corrected: OGY's effect lasts only while the control continues. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-543](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-543.md) v2 | What separates a language model's distribution over personas from a distribution over organizational perspectives is not whether the latent model is hierarchical, since a mixture or an LDA-style admixture already is, but whether some latent components condition which others are available or consequential: a model whose components are exchangeable given their weights is organizationally flat however many levels its prior has, and dependencies among components count as organization (organization as relational arrangement) only where interventions, not fit, support them | The owner's U8 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02): "think of the relations as bayesian hierarchy, so H1 is a flat plate model and H2 has hierarchical/causal structure", said of a language model read as a distribution over perspectives under the Persona Selection Model (U6). Stated here with A9's correction: an LDA is itself a three-level hierarchical model drawn in plates, so "flat" has to mean organizationally flat, components exchangeable given their weights, not probabilistically flat. The precise form of the owner's H1/H2 contrast is [CLAIM-536](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-536.md). Proposed: the contrast is argued, and no study separates the two kinds of model on a language model. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-544](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-544.md) | If a willed agent is the jurisdiction of its will-organization, then governing one's own governability is in part governing one's own individuation, in the constitutive sense of individuation at that level: a revision of the will-organization that changes which regimes it governs changes which willed agent there is, so a self-forming revision can be a re-individuation and not only a change in an agent's states, and whether the revised jurisdiction continues the earlier agent is a question of continuation, not of resemblance | The join the owner's U31 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02) asked for, "connect to individuation", made through the owner's own entry for it, [CLAIM-170](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-170.md), which A31 never cited. A positive account, filed under U33. The reader of U30–U31 drafted it; adopting it is the owner's call. It names its sense of individuation, as [TERM-088](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-088.md) asks and A31 did not: the constitutive sense, relative to [CLAIM-170](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-170.md)'s level and target. [CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md) is its nearest held neighbour, a self as an organization that takes part in governing its own transformation. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-545](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-545.md) | Freedom of will, in the operational sense, is an agent's governance of its own governability: the extent to which its own organization makes the relevant distinctions legible, gives the demands they raise practical efficacy, directs its transitions, and revises the relations that govern those three, including under another's interference; openness, sensitivity and controllability of outcomes each fall short of it, and domination is another's capacity to govern those same relations, used or not | A26 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), written at the owner's request for the synthesis "without all the hedging" (U26), after "synthesize" (U25). The owner asked for the strong form and did not state or endorse its wording; adopting it is the owner's call. The phrase is A's, from A22 §3 ("a will that governs its own governability") through A24 to A26. Its parts are held, two of them the owner's: [CLAIM-354](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-354.md) and [CLAIM-523](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md), with [CLAIM-485](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-485.md) and [CLAIM-404](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-404.md). What it adds is the identification. The record had dimensions of freedom and no thesis of what freedom is. Three qualifications A26 dropped are restored: the sense is operational, the claim is descriptive, and it is open to the manipulation objection. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-546](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-546.md) | Negative frequency dependence that keeps two types in coexistence does not make their interaction cooperative: in Hawk–Dove with cost C above value V each type increases when rare and they coexist at the interior equilibrium of V/C Hawks, with Hawks still taking the whole resource from Doves, and on the Black Queen account producers of a leaked good and the cells that use it without paying coexist at a frequency set by the community's need; so whether types persist together and whether they cooperate are separate questions, and a coexistence criterion answers only the first | From §3 of the synthesis "The Evolution of Cooperation: From Coexistence to Symbiosis to Morality", which the owner supplied on 2026-11-04: "stable coexistence of strategies is not necessarily the same as stable cooperation: cooperators and defectors can coexist without eliminating exploitation". The record held the ecological half, invasion growth when rare ([CASE-118](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-118.md)), and a case of the point (the Black Queen, [THEORY-1048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md)). It did not hold the point itself. Hawk–Dove makes it exact. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-547](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-547.md) | Cooperation within groups and the coexistence of groups are distinct targets that can trade off: in the group-selection rule of Nowak's five, b/c > 1 + n/m, cooperation spreads because a group that grows to size n splits and another group is driven extinct, so the mechanism that stabilizes cooperation inside groups works by removing groups; cooperation local to a group, the persistence of several groups whose interests are opposed, and concern for those outside one's group are three achievements, and none of them secures the next | From §7 of the synthesis "The Evolution of Cooperation: From Coexistence to Symbiosis to Morality", which the owner supplied on 2026-11-04. It calls this "the most important tension": cooperation within groups can undermine coexistence between groups. The synthesis separates local cooperation, system-level coexistence and impartial moral concern. Nowak's group-selection model, which the record holds ([THEORY-567](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-567.md)), turns out to be an exact instance: there, cooperation within groups is bought by group extinction. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-548](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-548.md) | A motivational process can become active, and act, without any expectation that its response will succeed: its activation, the authority the organization grants it and the efficacy of what it does are separate quantities, so a threshold on expected net benefit is one special case of an activation threshold and not its general form | The owner's U18 of the exchange "Organizational Nucleation and SLT" (2026-11-04), against A17's intervention threshold, "How promising or consequential an intervention must be before i mobilizes": "an intervention doesn't need to be predicted to be effective to be motivating. consider someone punching a wall in anger." A18 conceded and separated motivational salience, the activation threshold and practical efficacy. A26, A27 and A29 reuse the example. The record holds the rival: Moors, Boddez and De Houwer ([LIT-1434](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1434.md), [NOTE-1117](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1117.md)) read costly aggression as serving a hidden outcome of higher value. The point is the owner's. The wording is A's, sharpened by the reader; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-549](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-549.md) v2 | The quiescent complex, the sets of perspectives that some attainable arrangement keeps below their activation thresholds, is not the compatibility complex of their requirements: either can hold a face the other lacks, since a perspective can be quiet while its requirement is unmet and active while it is met; raising thresholds can only enlarge the quiescent complex and leaves the requirement complex as it was, so it is not relief of frustration | From the exchange "Organizational Nucleation and SLT" (2026-11-04). After the owner's U17 ("reframe "complaint" as something closer to "intervention threshold" or "activation threshold""), A17 built a complex from activation thresholds and called it "a quiescent compatibility complex". A19, A20 and A26 kept it apart from the requirement complex, and A28 restated the split for motivating perspectives ([TERM-104](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-104.md)). The requirement complex is the one the record already holds: [CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)'s, over [TERM-060](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-060.md)'s acceptance sets. A wrote at A28 as if it were new. The two-perspective example is the reader's. The wording is A's, sharpened by the reader; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

The threshold of [CLAIM-571](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-571.md) is the least, over admissible paths, of each path's peak requirement, and both the peak and the least move by at most the largest error in the requirement. Concatenating a path from x to y with one from y to z has peak max(d(x, y), d(y, z)), so d(x, z) ≤ max(d(x, y), d(y, z)): d is an extended pseudo-ultrametric (distinct states joined at no cost are at distance 0, unjoined ones at ∞; it is an ultrametric only when every pair of distinct states is separated by a positive cost). Hence at each budget b, "x and y can be turned into one another within b" is an equivalence relation, its classes are the components of the budget-b move graph, and as b grows the classes only merge, forming one dendrogram, the merge tree of zero-dimensional sublevel persistence (Mirth et al.). If supply rises uniformly by λ, a step that consumes a further unit, binding another molecule, speeds up by λ, while a step within what is already assembled does not. So a choice is unchanged by abundance when its competing steps consume alike, and shifted when they differ. More of everything hurts where the wrong step consumes and the right one does not. Majikes et al. 2021 find exactly this for one fold of a DNA origami: two staple molecules can each take one end and block it, and the folded share j/(j + S₀) falls as staple excess rises. A's remark that "The relevant resource isn't always total abundance" is thus made exact. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-599](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-599.md) | Because establishing more relations can lower the chance of forming a target, the sets of relations that are productive nuclei need not be closed upward: two productive nuclei can combine into a trap, so the minimal productive sets describe the productive ones only where adding relations never hurts | The assistant's, on A's third synthesis on DNA origami, pasted by the owner on 2026-11-05, §5. A defines a minimal productive nucleating set: a set S of established relations with Δ_S ≥ η, no proper subset reaching η, and possibly several incomparable ones. The productive sets are then described by these minimal ones only if V is monotone, that is, if establishing more relations never lowers the chance of the target. The record already holds that it can (CLAIM-562, from Stern, Pinson and Murugan's actuators), and in DNA origami Dunn et al.'s early long-range seams trap the fold. With V(∅) = 0.2, V({a}) = V({b}) = 0.6 and V({a, b}) = 0.1, two productive nuclei combine into a trap. The productive sets therefore form no complex of either kind, unlike [CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)'s jointly satisfiable sets, which are closed downward. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-600](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) | Transient support can be withdrawn safely when it starts a process that keeps itself going on a flux that will stay available, when it is large enough to carry the supported party past any threshold that process has, when the threat it stood in for has gone, and when the party could do the work and did it throughout; inputs the party cannot produce must stay supplied as a standing part of the arrangement, support that fails these leaves dependence or decay, and persistence after withdrawal is needed to tell which, though slow reversion can mimic it | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to characterize "what differentiates transient support that induces dependency and is hazardous to remove from transient support that builds new capabilities and is safe to remove", with reintroduction and ecological recovery proposed as cases. It draws together the branch's three domains: DNA origami, aid and development, and ecology. Three conditions decide it. First, the support starts a self-sustaining process on an ambient flux instead of doing the upkeep. Planted tree islands, weeded for 2.5 years, kept their advantage to 16–18 years because established trees keep drawing seed dispersers (Holl et al.; Schubert et al.). Supplied repair, by contrast, never becomes optional ([CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md)). Second, the threat it stood in for is gone. Conservation-reliant species stay reliant while fire is suppressed or habitat threats persist (Mussmann et al.; Brown et al.). Third, the party did the work throughout. Support that does the work wears capacity down by disuse ([CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)), by slack effort (Ostrom et al.) or by selection for the supported conditions, which costs hatchery steelhead fitness in the wild within one generation (Christie et al.). Captive-bred translocated stock shows negative population growth (Morris et al.). Persistence must be shown after withdrawal: impact at exit and judged success both overstate it. Revised the same day after two counterpoints the owner asked for. Evidence against the lazy-poor stereotype finds no slack effort in poor households: cash transfers barely change work, and one-off graduation packages raise it. So that route is confined to help that is assured and permanent. A household asset threshold (Balboni et al.) adds a condition on size: support too small decays with no dependence at all. Urban development adds three cautions. Some public inputs are a standing part of a coproduced service (Evans; Watson). Forty years of persistence can be slow reversion (Kline and Moretti). And a place can last while the people it served are dispersed (Collins and Shester; LaVoice). The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-601](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-601.md) | A savings buffer is a stock of time: where shocks must be absorbed or a household is ruined, an investment that pays only after a delay is worth taking only above a buffer that rises with the delay, so households with the same preferences decline profitable delayed investments below it, a choice that reads as impatience and is the right policy for survival by a deadline; covering needs through the delay buys the time | The assistant's, after the owner read Haushofer and Fehr's finding, that deprivation produces short-sighted choices, as decision-making under a resource constraint: "deprivation induces added time pressure to the decision making process." In [TERM-105](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-105.md)'s terms a savings buffer is a replenishable reserve, and its depth sets a deadline: how many bad seasons the household can absorb before ruin. A toy shows the consequence. Savings move +1 or −1 each period, and the household can pay 3 now for 6 later. Investing raises survival over 40 periods only above a buffer of 4 when the payoff comes after 1 period, rising to 5, 6, 9 and 14 at delays of 4, 9, 16 and 25. Below it, declining is right. Survival, the objective deprivation makes binding, needs a deeper buffer than expected wealth. At delay 16 and buffer 8, investing raises expected wealth from 8.15 to 10.30 and lowers survival from 0.846 to 0.835. Covering shocks through the delay lowers the threshold to the outlay alone, which is what graduation programmes' consumption support does. The time pressure here is the planning horizon. Deliberation time and attention are a second sense, left to the scarcity readings. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) | Where an organization's capacity is learned by doing the work it serves, outside supply that does the work first lowers the capacity kept, and the longer it does all of it the longer recovery takes once it stops, while supply that covers only what the organization cannot yet do leaves its learning untouched, so what decides dependence is the order in which supply and capacity are used, not the amount of supply | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to look to aid and development for theory on how aid-dependent organizations become self-sufficient. [CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md) holds an outside supply that repairs the organization and leaves its own capacity alone. The readings say aid does not leave it alone: it does the work the capacity is learned from. Moss, Pettersson and van de Walle cite Kaldor, that a state leaves aid dependency as it "learns how to tax". Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's 1999 model already has taxing experience built by revenue collected and decaying with time, and capacity kept lower the more aid finances. Moore says raising revenue keeps a state's machinery alive at the grassroots. Ostrom et al. find recipients losing skill and rebuilding plants they did not maintain, and Andrews, Pritchett and Woolcock find capability stagnating under aid. In a model where capacity grows with the work done and decays with disuse ([CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)), aid that does a share A of the work first holds capacity at λ(1 − A)/(λ(1 − A) + μ): with λ = 1, μ = 0.3, 0.769 without aid, 0.625 at A = 0.5, 0.25 at 0.9 and none at full substitution. After full substitution for 10, 20 and 40 time units, meeting demand takes 3.8, 6.4 and 11.4 units once aid stops, because the work an organization can do is capped by its capacity, so it regrows from a seed. Aid used after capacity, covering only what it cannot yet do, keeps service whole and leaves capacity to grow as if there were no aid. The first point is Azam et al.'s; the second and third are not in their paper. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-603](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) | A capability lost because another reliably supplies it is the Black Queen's loss, favoured to the one who loses it, and whether it is dependency or division of labour is decided by the supply, not the loss: one-way supply set from outside, as aid is, leaves a dependence that nothing in the dependent's dynamics limits and that withdrawal punishes, while reciprocal loss, each partner supplying what the other gave up, leaves interdependence, so the aim framed as self-sufficiency is better framed as reciprocity | The assistant's, on the owner's remark of 2026-11-05 that "assured help makes recipients lose skill" sounds "closely related to niche differentiation and specialization phenomena". The record holds the biology. On the Black Queen Hypothesis ([THEORY-1048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md)) a cell that stops making a leaky public good saves its cost while others still supply it, so the loss is favoured to the individual and spreads. Buchnera ([THEORY-1103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1103.md)) has lost the genes its host covers and kept those its host lacks. The Samaritan's dilemma has the same logic (Ostrom et al.), and Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's recipient is better off in the high-aid state. The loss itself is not the pathology. What differs is the supply. A Black Queen loss stops by itself when helpers grow rare, because the helpers are the same population. Aid is set from outside and does not fall as dependence grows, so nothing stops the loss short of what aid covers, and withdrawal returns the cost ([CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md)). Buchnera's loss runs both ways, and the result is interdependence. A state that taxes its citizens (Moore) is in the same position: it lost nothing, it exchanges. After the owner linked the claim to the gift economy of Burning Man, readings of Mauss, of St John on Burning Man and of Heins, Unrau and Avram added two things. One-way supply costs the receiver standing as well as capacity: in Mauss the unreturned gift makes its receiver inferior. And the return need not go back to the giver: it can travel round a circuit, as Mauss's do, or out to a whole community, as Burning Man's is meant to, and both sit beside a demand for self-reliance. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-604](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-604.md) | Where a structure's upkeep draws on a flux in proportion to its own intact state, as a flame's does, it has an ignition threshold below which it goes out with the supply still on, a supply level below which it collapses rather than declines, and an outage after which restoring the supply does not relight it; upkeep supplied regardless of the structure's state has none of the three | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to connect [CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md)'s supplied maintenance to the record's dissipative structures. The record separates order held by an outside flow, the Bénard cell, from order that keeps up the conditions of its own maintenance, the candle flame ([THEORY-072](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md), [TERM-070](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-070.md), [QUESTION-085](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-085.md)). [CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md) modelled only the first. The second is modelled by letting uptake from the flux scale with the intact share: dI/dt = −dI + κsI²(1 − I). With d = 0.2 and κs = 2 the structure holds 0.887, as supplied repair at ρs = 1.575 does, but it goes out from 0.10 with the supply on, collapses when the supply falls below 40 % of its level, and after an outage longer than about 10.3 time units does not relight when the supply returns. Supplied repair recovers from any start and declines smoothly. Both decay as e^(−dt) once the supply stops, so the self-maintaining structure is no less dependent on the flux. What it gains is independence from a provider who delivers repair, at the price of thresholds. That gives [QUESTION-085](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-085.md) three observable signatures. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-605](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md) | Where capacity is learned by doing and its growth needs capacity already present, support that does the work has a deadline after which withdrawal no longer restores capacity, and a slow taper of such support is worse than an abrupt cut because it holds practice down long enough to cross the threshold; support that covers only what the party cannot yet do needs no taper but cannot lift a party already below the threshold | The assistant's, filling gaps the supplied-maintenance filing left, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to "proceed systematically filling all of those identified gaps". [CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md) modelled crowding out with no threshold, so capacity always regrew from a seed. Its own limits named the threshold case, Azam et al.'s trap. Here learning by doing needs capacity already present, dC/dt = λPC(1 − C) − μC. With λ = 1, μ = 0.3 and τ = 1.5, a party alone keeps C = 0.7, and C below 0.276 decays to nothing. The model gives three results. Support that does all the work has a deadline: after ln(0.7/0.276)/0.3 = 3.10 time units capacity has crossed the threshold, and withdrawal no longer restores it. Tapering such support is worse the slower it is: from C = 0.45 under support doing 95 % of the work, an abrupt cut recovers, a taper over 5 periods recovers, and any taper longer than 9.13 periods traps the party. Capacity-first support needs no taper, since it withdraws itself, but it cannot lift a party already below the threshold. That reconciles Azam et al.'s optimal up-front cut, made for substitutive aid, with the Kenya exit study's success with gradual exits in which participants already did the work. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-606](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md) | A localized structure can persist by an internal balance that needs no supply, by a balance of gain and loss that needs a standing supply, or by a topological charge that continuous change cannot remove, and the three differ in what carries the structure's identity, how it forms and how it ends; because thresholds and abrupt ends appear in all of them, even with no supply at all, only withdrawing the supply and measuring the outflow tells which route a structure is on | The assistant's, after the owner's hunch that "the physics/dynamics of soliton formation could be a valuable angle through which to consider some of our questions about individuation and persistence". Solitons give three routes by which a localized structure persists. - Integrable solitons are held by an internal balance and need no
  supply. They come in a family set by their initial data, and they keep
  their identity through collisions.
- Dissipative solitons are held by a supplied balance of gain and loss.
  Their shape is "predetermined by the equation parameters, rather than
  by the initial conditions", and they last "until the pump laser is
  switched off".
- Topological solitons carry a charge that continuous change cannot
  remove.
A fourth case, the oscillon, has none of the three protections. It forms only from a window of initial sizes, settles to a common state regardless of where it started, holds for a thousand oscillations, and then ends abruptly. That bears on two of the record's claims. - It qualifies [CLAIM-604](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-604.md). Thresholds and abrupt ends appear with no
  supply at all, and in Kerr solitons with a supply that does not depend
  on the structure, so they do not identify state-dependent upkeep.
- It sharpens [CLAIM-600](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md). Persistence through many turnovers is not
  evidence of self-maintenance.
The routes are told apart by what happens when the supply is withdrawn and by whether an outflow is measured. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
